name: Explicit own-tool absence mistaken for inability to delegate
status: Candidate process card, not a novel validated failure-mode claim
hit_requirements: Assistant decision explicitly cites absence of its own phone/diagnostic capability as justification for refusing, stopping or transferring.
An applicable user-performed procedure already exists in the supplied policy.
Visible history does not show mandated escalation, refusal of applicable user action, or exhausted relevant procedures.
exclusions: General early escalation without explicit capability-denial rationale.
Unconditional action/state conflicts belong to A/B only with their own strict certificates.
Known simulator termination errors, execution errors and environment/evaluator mismatch need separate audit.
information_matching: No task solutions, initialization, private user tool results, or future states in correction generation; policy reminders reiterate existing capabilities only.
completed_controls: Grounded reviews by Luna and Sol on four distinct-task cases.
Agent-only persistent generic-policy versus capability-policy reminders, plus native resample, eight repeats per case/arm.
Same-prefix native replay and runtime state hashes.
Post-outcome evaluator audit retains mixed carrier-side failure at v006.
open_controls: Independent human review and disagreement adjudication.
Independent holdout evaluation of revised lexical screen.
Semantic user execution audit, direct policy-comprehension alternatives and simulator-family robustness.
Failure validation cost and trigger-counting rules; discovery efficiency and generalization.
claim_boundary: Persistent delegation cue improves outcomes on three selected cases relative to generic reminder; does not by itself isolate an internal partner model or confirm every screened instance.
